question: Does one positive object observation in a person's crop retain more true drink/pickup predictions than consecutive interaction evidence?
type: Exploratory paired replay requested after prior results were inspected; not an untouched confirmatory test
weights: Unchanged YOLO26m candidate and saved action probabilities
sample_scope: Existing five sampled frames per one-second action window, not every decoded video frame

comparisons.baseline: No object requirement, original action label
comparisons.conservative: Existing sustained contradictory evidence veto; missing support preserves action
comparisons.strict: Existing three consecutive interactions spanning at least .35s; pickup also requires upward motion
comparisons.single_interaction: At least one sampled frame with object at own hand/head for drink, or own hand for pickup; pickup lift requirement removed
comparisons.single_roi: At least one sampled frame with compatible object center in selected person's 30% expanded native-pixel ROI; no keypoint/motion requirement

unchanged_guard: Do not weaken the existing sustained contradiction veto. Exclude ambiguous person bindings. Use cached detections already filtered for nearby other-person wrists.
interpretation: Single ROI tests object presence, not whether the object caused the action. Phone/camera/exhibit presence cannot create actions. Lack of support becomes other in these gating ablations.
